prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1450; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver regarding a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle entered the intersection on a red signal and struck the driver's passenger side door. Police report requested and reference number logged. Vehicle is drivable but has been taken to a body shop for estimate.

Entry 2: Contacted the claimant by phone. Claimant confirms no attorney retained and states they prefer to handle the claim directly. Claimant reports neck and back strain following the collision and says they were evaluated at an urgent care clinic. Advised claimant of the medical payments coverage available under the policy and requested copies of all treatment records and bills.

Entry 3: Received the police report. It notes the other driver was cited for failure to obey a traffic control device. Both drivers gave consistent accounts of the signal phase. Witness statement not included in the report. Liability appears clear in favor of the insured, pending receipt of the other carrier's position.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant about symptoms. Claimant describes ongoing stiffness in the neck and lower back, limited sleep, and difficulty lifting. Claimant has scheduled a follow-up with their primary care provider. Explained the claims process and that a settlement offer cannot be made until treatment concludes and records are reviewed. Claimant indicated understanding.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. Repair estimate reviewed and found consistent with the damage pattern from a side impact. Subrogation notice sent to the at-fault carrier. Claim remains open pending medical documentation and final repair invoice. Diary set for follow-up with the claimant in two weeks.
